# DML write boundaries

## RUN-FACTS

- API 62.0 started at 07:27:11 UTC and API 67.0 at 07:28:14 UTC on 2026-11-25.
- Salesforce CLI 2.159.7 deployed the synthetic project to two fresh Developer scratch orgs from different Dev Hubs. Both scratch org deletions were verified.
- Each class and trigger used the API version in its row. Each anonymous run used that version for the CLI request and called the versioned probe class. The named route ran the three `@IsTest` methods synchronously.
- The probe permission set was assigned before either route. An anonymous debug marker and an intentional terminal assertion in each named method carried the observations. The exporter decoded the CLI's escaped pipe characters and masked the synthetic lookup ID in the error. Blank brackets and spaces are significant.
- Both API versions and both routes returned the same result for every primary case.

- The checked-in source was deployed again at 07:31:03 UTC and 07:32:08 UTC, respectively, to two fresh scratch orgs. These runs confirmed all prior rows and added the wrong-type lookup message, overlength key message and before-insert trigger count. Both scratch org deletions were verified.

## NEIGHBOR PROBES

- Existing, omitted and soft-deleted lookup targets are controls. Self lookups, required lookups, master-detail, lookup updates, and sparse local schemas keep their existing rules. The separate custom lookup capture covers absent standard parents.
- The overlong non-key field and deleted parent are controls for attempted-insert upsert failures. The separate external-ID capture covers scalar, padded and supplementary-character keys. Matching-key updates, standard ID-lookup selectors, explicit IDs, access-level overloads and REST responses were outside this supplemental capture.
- The text cases record caller, stored and trigger values. The fix covers Text, Text Area, and Long Text Area when Apex inserts and updates invoke before triggers. The partial external-ID upsert capture checks non-key values on inserted rows.
